title: Preserve production runtime settings while allowing development overrides
goal: Keep production runtime settings reproducible while intentionally overriding duplicate host configuration properties during development, especially when moving from a .NET 10 host to .NET 11.

selectionNotes: Use for .NET 11 host precedence; the .NET 10 consumer is a measured comparison, not a new target-10 foundation.

runtime.name: .NET
runtime.reason: The native host parser changes duplicate configProperties precedence in .NET 11 Preview 6; identify hostfxr separately from the application target.

sdk.name: .NET SDK
sdk.reason: Builds the example; exact SDK pins and generation/copy behavior are recorded separately.

language.name: C#
language.reason: C# 15 sample mode; the host configuration change itself is language independent.

platforms: CoreCLR supported platforms; actual host and artifact execution verified on Windows x64 only.
prerequisites: Build with the intended SDK and run with an explicitly identified hostfxr/runtime; PowerShell 7 for the authoring check.
constraints: Host runtimeOptions.configProperties only; no application-provider, Native AOT or universal publish-exclusion contract.
Deploy an inspected artifact set into a fresh directory; the three-file allowlist is valid only for this dependency-free sample.
stabilityLimitations: Measured .NET 11 RC2 is not GA evidence; no experimental API or native workload is required.

evidence.scope: Actual build and managed report execution; exact host behavior is separately verified in the execution record.
Real isolated hostfxr/runtime precedence, nonduplicate merge, absent dev file, source regeneration, SDK generation/copy and production artifact execution; Windows x64 only.
